heroHeadline: Slovakia Approves ~101 Troops and New 3D Radars for Poland, Romania Under NATO's Eastern Sentry
heroSubtitle: Slovakia's government approved deploying up to 101 Slovak Armed Forces personnel and new 3D radar systems (detection range roughly 350 km) to Poland and Romania to reinforce NATO's Eastern Sentry vigilance mission. Defence Minister Robert Kaliňák said Slovakia wants to 'test these radar systems in real-world conditions' while helping 'protect the airspace of our allies'; Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called it 'an important contribution to the security of NATO's eastern flank.' No new airspace incursions, intercepts, or shootdowns were reported across Poland, Romania, the Baltic states, or Germany between August 26–29, following the third explosive-drone find at Leipzig/Halle Airport and Latvia's confirmation that the August 14 Rugāji shootdown involved a Ukrainian-origin drone, both reported earlier this week.
footerNote: Data sourced from official NATO/SHAPE and member-state defense ministry statements, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
